title: The Choosing Isn't
concept: An AI agent can write up Alaska's whole public record, so the film makes writing physical and abundant (a round typewriter-press spewing curling reams) against ONE scarce square box, the LEAD slot, and asks who fills it.

fingerprint.palette: warm sunlit newsprint cream, spruce, bright daylight sky, one cadmium amber accent for the top slot
fingerprint.metaphor: an endless paper avalanche and one square box at the top that only a choice can fill

palette: warm sunlit newsprint cream, spruce, bright daylight sky, one cadmium amber accent for the top slot
divergence_note: First daylight film in three. 10-02 was a night lamplit brass bench in cross-section with a radial rack-focus, a brass counter and a question plate; 09-30 a night top-down collage traverse. This one is eye-level and vertical, the camera rising with a paper avalanche to a single square slot, in newsprint cream and spruce with one amber accent, the light itself carrying the argument (flat daylight for writing, one hard sun shaft on the slot for choosing). No counter: the ream height is the count. The open question is a kraft price tag, not a plate. New hero (NewsAgent, a writing machine), new throughline (LeadSlot), new sets (newsroom wall, home office, ambulance bay, council chamber, belt, dune, masthead wall).

angle.thesis: Walter shows that writing up Alaska's public record is now cheap, and the scarce work in local news has moved to choosing which records lead and saying plainly what they mean for readers.
angle.falsifiability: False if the criticisms of Walter's output were about factual errors, invented figures or missing material instead of what to lead with and how to frame it.
supporting_facts: c4 + c2 the platform ingests meetings, notices and filings, and Alaska News says it has published more than 4,500 stories
c10 + c11 Herz says it can't sort wheat from chaff, Walter answers hierarchy, not throughput
c13 the EMS headline was correct but unclear, Walter says it should have said plainly whether medics can use it yet
angle.counter_point: Walter makes no calls, attends no meetings, interviews nobody (c12), so reporting still takes people. Some stories publish with no human before and the editor checks afterward (c5). Herz, editor of a competing outlet, says reporters who ignore AI's value are burying their heads in the sand (c9, c16).
angle.second_movement: c7 + c8 the Press reports the founders' political and government ties, and Walter itself calls that a real trust burden, which makes the choosing layer where reader trust is won or lost. Walter's own line raises it, the film never asserts bias.

runner_ups.why_lost: implies bias through c7 and treats capability as a threat
treats the 4,500 self-count as achievement and skips c5

treatment.why: Strongest cold open, both loops planted on time, Herz's pro-AI line at full strength in Act 3, founders only through Walter's own words, few sets.
grafts: EXPLAINER winnowing sieve where everything falls through equally
EXPLAINER 4,500 as nine reams stamped ALASKA NEWS SAYS
COMEDIAN conveyor NO HUMAN BEFORE to CHECKED AFTER
DRAMATIST hang-tag question, here a price tag, flipped on the turn and kept apart from the founders plates
COMEDIAN moose head in the sand, labelled as the reporters Herz describes, never as Herz
treatment.judge_reasoning: Scorer: ENTHUSIAST 8.1, EXPLAINER 7.6, DRAMATIST 7.4, COMEDIAN 6.2. Fairness and the 60 to 95 test first, then retention and feasibility. Walter cast as a net-new writing machine rather than the shelf server box. Gate 0 revisions: named people are plates only with no hands, founders plates on the masthead away from the slot, Walter never in the council room, the dashed box empty until the button.

hook.frame1: The camera rising off a lip of paper toward an empty boxed LEAD slot on a daylight newsroom wall, sheets fluttering past.
hook.headline: WRITING THE NEWS GOT CHEAP
hook.loopback: The button pulls back to the same slot, fills it with one plain question, and the hatch clanks and drops a new stub, frame 1 again.
